title: New strict_spawn_class helper individually deletes temp_allocator slices — odin test emits 136 'bad free' diagnostics
evidence:
core/growth_test.odin:527-528:
	parent := make([]i32, n, context.temp_allocator)
	defer delete(parent)
core/growth_test.odin:556-557:
	size := make([]i32, n, context.temp_allocator)
	defer delete(size)

Running the project's own gate command (`odin test core`, ci-local.sh gate "Core unit tests") emits 136 diagnostics, e.g.:
	+++ bad free        @ 0x4D1800160 [growth_test.odin:528:strict_spawn_class()]
	+++ bad free        @ 0x4D1800148 [growth_test.odin:528:strict_spawn_class()]
	+++ bad free        @ 0x4D18006EC [growth_test.odin:557:strict_spawn_class()]
while finishing "232 tests ... All tests were successful." (Odin's test runner counts bad frees as errors only under FAIL_ON_BAD_MEMORY, core/testing/runner.odin:179-186, default false; its temp allocator is a per-thread Rollback_Stack that only supports free_all). The repo convention elsewhere never deletes temp-allocated slices, e.g. core/routing.odin:150-153:
	dist := make([]i32, int(n), context.temp_allocator)    // dist-to-dst per node slot (cost units)
	settled := make([]bool, int(n), context.temp_allocator) // settled per node slot
	seen := make([]bool, int(n), context.temp_allocator)    // per-(u,d) neighbor dedup
	min_cost := make([]i32, int(n), context.temp_allocator) // per-(u,d) neighbor MIN edge cost
(no delete calls; reclaimed by free_all(context.temp_allocator)).
detail: Temp-allocator memory freed via per-slice delete is an invalid free under the test runner's rollback-stack temp allocator: 136 bad-free reports pollute every `odin test core` run and would fail the suite under ODIN_TEST_FAIL_ON_BAD_MEMORY=true, undermining the 'local test suite green' acceptance evidence.
recommended_fix: Drop both `defer delete` lines (n is tiny; record_run's free_all and the runner's per-test rollback reclaim the temp memory), matching core/routing.odin's temp-scratch convention — or allocate both slices via context.allocator so make/delete pair.
